title: Count Subarrays With Cost Less Than or Equal to K
summary: Given an integer array nums and an integer k, count the number of subarrays where the cost, defined as the difference between the maximum and minimum values of the subarray multiplied by its length, is less than or equal to k.
statement: Given an integer array nums and an integer k, count the number of subarrays where the cost, defined as the difference between the maximum and minimum values of the subarray multiplied by its length, is less than or equal to k.
constraints: nums has up to 100,000 integers and k is nonnegative.
A subarray of length L costs (maximum-minimum)×L.
Count all nonempty contiguous subarrays whose cost is at most k.
hints: For a fixed right endpoint, removing values from the left cannot increase range or length.
Maintain window maximum and minimum with decreasing and increasing index deques.
Shrink until the cost qualifies, then add every suffix starting from left through right.
Monotonicity makes exactly right-left+1 suffixes valid, and each index enters and leaves each deque once.
editorial: Monotonicity makes exactly right-left+1 suffixes valid, and each index enters and leaves each deque once.

tests.explanation: All subarrays except [1,3,2] qualify, so the count is five.
Both singletons and the equal pair have zero cost, giving three.
